By the end of this lesson I will be able to

  • Name six physical methods for separating mixtures.
  • Explain which property each method uses.
  • Carry out separations at the practical stations.
  • Choose a method to separate a new mixture.
The big ideaThe parts of a mixture are NOT chemically joined, so we can separate them using a difference in a property: size, weight, magnetism or how they stick to things.
SafetyKeep the magnet in its bag. Do not blow sand or filings: use the fan only at Station 2. Goggles at Stations 2 and 3. Wash your hands after touching oil or iron filings.
Your bookRecord with a table, drawings or a photo journal. Rate each station: ★ poor, ★★ OK, ★★★ very well.

Key terms, spell them correctly: sieving · winnowing · magnetic separation · sedimentation · decantation · filtration · residue · filtrate · adsorption
Notes

Muddy water is a heterogeneous mixture of soil and water. Because the parts of a mixture are NOT chemically joined, we can separate them using their different properties: size, weight, magnetism, or how they stick to things.

Six separation methods

8 – 20 min · Task 2 · Criterion A
MethodProperty usedExample
SievingSize of solid piecesStones from sand
WinnowingWeight (light vs heavy)Husks from grain
MagnetismMagnetic or notIron from sand
DecantationHeavy solid sinksMuddy water
FiltrationSize: liquid or dissolved vs insoluble solidSand from water
Oil adsorptionOil sticks to the sawdust surfaceOil spill on water

STEP 3 · TEST

Practical: separation stations

20 – 40 min · Task 3 · Criterion C
  • Station 1 · Sieving: shake sand + small stones through the sieve over a bowl.
  • Station 2 · Winnowing: gently toss the grain on a tray while a partner fans it.
  • Station 3 · Magnetism: move the bagged magnet over sand + iron filings, then lift it and remove the bag over a dish.
  • Station 4 · Decantation: without shaking, slowly pour the top water off settled muddy water. Stop before the mud moves.
  • Station 5 · Filtration: fold filter paper into a cone in a funnel and pour muddy water through.
  • Station 6 · Oil adsorption: sprinkle sawdust over oil on water, wait 1 minute, then scoop the oily sawdust out.

This step: 2 marks
STEP 4 · EXPLAIN

Why each method works

40 – 50 min · Task 4 · Criterion A
  • Every method uses a DIFFERENCE in a property between the parts of the mixture.
  • Filtration: water particles are small enough to pass through the tiny holes in filter paper; sand grains are too big.
  • Filtration does NOT remove dissolved substances such as salt: salt particles are too small and pass through with the water.
  • Adsorption: oil sticks to the huge surface of the many tiny sawdust pieces. Hardwood sawdust (like oak) holds oil well and floats, so it can be collected.
▶ Ocean oil spill simulation and clean-up (TheDadLab, 1:43)Try it at home with oil, water and a sponge
